what_this_is: The 0.1 -> 0.2 migration check, not a new result. Qwen3.8-27B on the pinned SparkInfer commit, batch 1, ctx 128, three interleaved pairs, one RTX 5090 -- run through the MIGRATED stack: namespace tensortransit, adapters/sparkinfer, the TENSORTRANSIT_ environment prefix, and the CMake package TensorTransit. It exists to answer one question: did generalizing RecurLocal into TensorTransit change what the recurrent policy does? It did not. +0.13% against a 0.06% noise floor is the figure 0.1 published for this arm (README, 'First real result'), and the token-exact gate passes with the control reproducible over three unhooked replays. This is a PARTIAL matrix -- batch 1 only, 0.40 of the section 44 weight -- so decide.py will not call it significant, which is correct and is the point of running it as a check rather than as a submission.

workload_coverage.why: Section 44 weights batch 1 at 0.40 and concurrency at 0.60. An arm that was not run is left out of the matrix rather than filled in, and the weights that remain are renormalised by decide.py - so a partial run is reported as a partial verdict instead of a full one with invented halves.

resolution.note: resolved=false means the difference is inside the run-to-run spread of the runs that produced it, whichever way it points

measurement.note: resolved=false means the difference is inside the control arm's own run-to-run spread on this box; the axis is open, not settled.

note_on_scope: Do NOT quote this as a TensorTransit result. It is the recurrent_v0 policy family, whose weighted ceiling is 0.52% on this model and 1.94% on the best model found -- both below the 2.0% floor. See README and docs/MINING.md.
